1	Temperature-sensitive payloads such as medicines, diagnostic samples, and perishable foods are frequently distributed in insulated containers that carry their own thermal reserve. A container of this kind is loaded at a packing point, handed to one or more carriers, and opened at a destination that may be many hours away. Because the container travels unattended and often without electrical power, the thermal behaviour of the container has to be set at the moment of closing and cannot be corrected in transit.
2	
3	Two practical difficulties dominate the use of such containers. The first is the distribution of cold within the payload space. A thermal reserve placed against one wall, or laid directly on top of a payload, cools the material nearest to it strongly and the material farthest from it weakly, so the payload experiences a spread of temperatures. Direct contact between the thermal reserve and the payload can drive the contacted items below the intended range while more distant items drift above it. Moving air distributes the effect of the reserve more evenly, but a fan, pump, or other powered air mover adds a battery, a failure mode, and a service burden, and is unwelcome in a container that has to be returned and used again.
4	
5	The second difficulty is that a container which relies on an internal air path only performs as intended if that path is actually present when the container is closed. Loose internal components are lifted, rotated, or nudged during loading and during transport. If the passages that are supposed to carry conditioned air downward are displaced relative to the passages that are supposed to carry it back, the intended path is broken and the container behaves as an ordinary insulated box, without any outward sign that anything is wrong. Placing that responsibility on the person who packs the container is unreliable, because a component that is merely set in place looks the same whether or not it is correctly positioned.
6	
7	Related handling problems arise in reusable service. Condensate forms on cold surfaces inside a closed container and collects where it is difficult to reach. Removing it commonly means handling the thermal reserve itself, which is undesirable when the reserve is a phase-change cassette that should not be opened in the field. Finally, a payload that has been briefly warmed can arrive at a temperature that appears correct, so a recipient inspecting the container at delivery cannot tell from the contents alone whether the thermal reserve lost its condition earlier in the journey.
8	
9	There remains a need for a reusable passive carrier in which the internal circulation path is established positively by the act of closing the container, in which the thermal reserve is held in that established relationship during transport, and in which routine servicing and evidence of thermal exposure are available without opening the thermal reserve.
10

1	In the following description, the terms upper, lower, above, below, inward, and outward refer to the carrier in its normal upright attitude of use, in which the insulated lid is uppermost. The described embodiments illustrate the invention and do not limit it. FIG. 1 through FIG. 6 show one carrier, each view showing the parts that view is concerned with, and a part introduced in one view is referred to elsewhere in this description whether or not it is shown in every view.
2	
3	## Overview of the carrier
4	
5	Referring to FIG. 1, FIG. 2, and FIG. 5, a reusable passive cold-chain carrier includes an insulated outer shell 10, a removable product tray 20, a removable thermal module 40, and an insulated lid 60. The insulated outer shell 10 has a shell floor 12, shell side walls 14 rising from the shell floor 12, and an upper edge 16 at the top of the shell side walls 14. The insulated outer shell 10 and the insulated lid 60 are of insulating construction, and the carrier can be returned for reuse.
6	
7	Referring also to FIG. 5, the removable product tray 20 receives the payload. The removable product tray 20 has tray side walls 24 and tray feet 22. The tray feet 22 stand on the shell floor 12 and suspend the removable product tray 20 above the shell floor 12, so that a lower return passage 28 remains under the removable product tray 20. The tray side walls 24 are spaced inward from the shell side walls 14 to form two side supply passages 30. The removable product tray 20 has perforations 26 through the removable product tray 20.
8	
9	The removable product tray 20 lifts out of the insulated outer shell 10 as a unit, with the payload in it, once the removable thermal module 40 has been taken out. Loading and unloading therefore do not disturb the passages, because the passages are formed by the position that the removable product tray 20 takes up when it is returned to the insulated outer shell 10 and not by any separate ducting that has to be assembled.
10	
11	## The removable thermal module
12	
13	Referring to FIG. 1, FIG. 3, and FIG. 4, the removable thermal module 40 includes a rigid spacer frame 42 holding two opposed phase-change cassettes 44. The rigid spacer frame 42 is a rigid frame body. The rigid spacer frame 42 rests above the removable product tray 20 and below the insulated lid 60, so that the removable thermal module 40 is lifted out as one piece and the two phase-change cassettes 44 travel with it.
14	
15	The rigid spacer frame 42 includes a central inlet opening 46 at the centre of the rigid spacer frame 42 and facing the product region within the removable product tray 20, two downward guide ducts 48 beside the phase-change cassettes 44, and peripheral outlet openings 50. Each phase-change cassette 44 is a cassette of phase-change material that is conditioned before use, and the two phase-change cassettes 44 are held on opposite sides of the central inlet opening 46 with their faces mutually opposed. Each downward guide duct 48 extends downward beside one of the phase-change cassettes 44 and opens at its lower end. The peripheral outlet openings 50 lie at the periphery of the rigid spacer frame 42 and are aligned with the side supply passages 30 when the removable thermal module 40 is in a registered position.
16	
17	Because the two phase-change cassettes 44 are opposed and are held apart by the rigid spacer frame 42, the air that enters between them is exposed to two cooled faces at once.
18	
19	## The registered passive circulation path
20	
21	The carrier is passive. It has no fan, pump, or powered air mover. Circulation is produced by the density difference between the air warmed by the payload and the air cooled at the faces of the phase-change cassettes 44, and the geometry of the carrier gives that difference a single closed path to follow.
22	
23	In use, warm air rising from a product region within the removable product tray 20 enters the central inlet opening 46, divides along faces of the phase-change cassettes 44, descends through the downward guide ducts 48, enters the side supply passages 30, passes through the perforations 26 in the removable product tray 20, and returns through the lower return passage 28 to the product region. The path is closed on itself and surrounds the removable product tray 20 on the sides and underneath, so that cooled air reaches the payload around and beneath the removable product tray 20.
24	
25	The path exists only when the peripheral outlet openings 50 overlap the side supply passages 30. In the following description, the terms upper, lower, above, below, inward, and outward refer to the carrier in its normal upright attitude of use, in which the insulated lid is uppermost. The described embodiments illustrate the invention and do not limit it. FIG. 1 through FIG. 6 show one carrier, each view showing the parts that view is concerned with, and a part introduced in one view is referred to elsewhere in this description whether or not it is shown in every view.

## Overview of the carrier

Referring to FIG. 1, FIG. 2, and FIG. 5, a reusable passive cold-chain carrier includes an insulated outer shell 10, a removable product tray 20, a removable thermal module 40, and an insulated lid 60. The insulated outer shell 10 has a shell floor 12, shell side walls 14 rising from the shell floor 12, and an upper edge 16 at the top of the shell side walls 14. The insulated outer shell 10 and the insulated lid 60 are of insulating construction, and the carrier can be returned for reuse.

Referring also to FIG. 5, the removable product tray 20 receives the payload. The removable product tray 20 has tray side walls 24 and tray feet 22. The tray feet 22 stand on the shell floor 12 and suspend the removable product tray 20 above the shell floor 12, so that a lower return passage 28 remains under the removable product tray 20. The tray side walls 24 are spaced inward from the shell side walls 14 to form two side supply passages 30. The removable product tray 20 has perforations 26 through the removable product tray 20.

The removable product tray 20 lifts out of the insulated outer shell 10 as a unit, with the payload in it, once the removable thermal module 40 has been taken out. Loading and unloading therefore do not disturb the passages, because the passages are formed by the position that the removable product tray 20 takes up when it is returned to the insulated outer shell 10 and not by any separate ducting that has to be assembled.

## The removable thermal module

Referring to FIG. 1, FIG. 3, and FIG. 4, the removable thermal module 40 includes a rigid spacer frame 42 holding two opposed phase-change cassettes 44. The rigid spacer frame 42 is a rigid frame body. The rigid spacer frame 42 rests above the removable product tray 20 and below the insulated lid 60, so that the removable thermal module 40 is lifted out as one piece and the two phase-change cassettes 44 travel with it.

The rigid spacer frame 42 includes a central inlet opening 46 at the centre of the rigid spacer frame 42 and facing the product region within the removable product tray 20, two downward guide ducts 48 beside the phase-change cassettes 44, and peripheral outlet openings 50. Each phase-change cassette 44 is a cassette of phase-change material that is conditioned before use, and the two phase-change cassettes 44 are held on opposite sides of the central inlet opening 46 with their faces mutually opposed. Each downward guide duct 48 extends downward beside one of the phase-change cassettes 44 and opens at its lower end. The peripheral outlet openings 50 lie at the periphery of the rigid spacer frame 42 and are aligned with the side supply passages 30 when the removable thermal module 40 is in a registered position.

Because the two phase-change cassettes 44 are opposed and are held apart by the rigid spacer frame 42, the air that enters between them is exposed to two cooled faces at once.

## The registered passive circulation path

The carrier is passive. It has no fan, pump, or powered air mover. Circulation is produced by the density difference between the air warmed by the payload and the air cooled at the faces of the phase-change cassettes 44, and the geometry of the carrier gives that difference a single closed path to follow.

In use, warm air rising from a product region within the removable product tray 20 enters the central inlet opening 46, divides along faces of the phase-change cassettes 44, descends through the downward guide ducts 48, enters the side supply passages 30, passes through the perforations 26 in the removable product tray 20, and returns through the lower return passage 28 to the product region. The path is closed on itself and surrounds the removable product tray 20 on the sides and underneath, so that cooled air reaches the payload around and beneath the removable product tray 20.

The path exists only when the peripheral outlet openings 50 overlap the side supply passages 30. If the removable thermal module 40 is set down out of position, the peripheral outlet openings 50 discharge against the tray side walls 24 or against the shell side walls 14, the descending limb of the path is blocked, and the carrier behaves as a plain insulated box. This is the failure that the registration described below is directed to, and it is a failure that gives no outward sign, because a removable thermal module 40 that is merely set in place looks the same whether or not it is correctly positioned.

## Lid-driven registration and retention

Referring to FIG. 1 and FIG. 3, the insulated lid 60 carries a depending indexing rib 62, and the rigid spacer frame 42 has a mating channel 52 that receives the depending indexing rib 62. As the insulated lid 60 closes, the depending indexing rib 62 enters the mating channel 52 and shifts the removable thermal module 40 into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings 50 overlap the side supply passages 30. The registration is therefore performed by the act of closing the carrier. The person who packs the carrier is not required to align the removable thermal module 40, and cannot leave it misaligned, because the insulated lid 60 does not come down onto the upper edge 16 without carrying the removable thermal module 40 into position.

A compressible lid gasket 64 on the insulated lid 60 seals against the upper edge 16 of the insulated outer shell 10 after registration. The order of these two events matters. The depending indexing rib 62 engages the mating channel 52 and completes the registration before the compressible lid gasket 64 seals against the upper edge 16, so that the removable thermal module 40 is free to be shifted by the depending indexing rib 62 and is not being asked to move after the interior has been closed off. Only then does continued closing compress the compressible lid gasket 64 against the upper edge 16 and seal the interior.

Referring to FIG. 4, the same closing movement presses resilient feet 54 of the rigid spacer frame 42 against ledges 18 of the insulated outer shell 10, so that the removable thermal module 40 cannot lift away from the removable product tray 20 during transport. That pressing holds the removable thermal module 40 down against handling, tilting, and vibration in transit, which would otherwise let the removable thermal module 40 rise and break the overlap between the peripheral outlet openings 50 and the side supply passages 30.

Registration and retention are thus produced by the same movement that a user has to make in any event. Nothing has to be latched, clamped, or checked separately, and there is no state in which the carrier is closed and sealed but the circulation path is not established.

## Condensate handling and the removable wick

Referring to FIG. 4 and FIG. 5, a shallow condensate channel 70 extends around the removable product tray 20, and a removable absorbent wick 72 lies in the shallow condensate channel 70. Condensate discharge openings 56 at lower ends of the downward guide ducts 48 discharge condensate into the shallow condensate channel 70. Moisture that condenses on the cooled surfaces within the downward guide ducts 48 runs down the ducts and leaves them through the condensate discharge openings 56, rather than collecting on the payload or standing in the bottom of the interior.

The removable absorbent wick 72 has a pull tab 74. The pull tab 74 remains accessible when the removable product tray 20 is removed, so that the removable absorbent wick 72 is drawn out of the shallow condensate channel 70 and replaced without opening a phase-change cassette 44. Routine servicing between journeys therefore does not require handling of the phase-change cassettes 44, which are conditioned items and are not to be opened. Withdrawing the removable absorbent wick 72 from the shallow condensate channel 70 by the pull tab 74 and placing a replacement absorbent wick in the shallow condensate channel 70 restores the carrier for the next journey.

## Mechanical exposure indicator

Referring to FIG. 6, the insulated outer shell 10 includes a mechanical exposure indicator 80 visible from outside. An indicator stem 82 is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette 44 and is retained by a temperature-responsive latch 84. A spring 86 acts on the indicator stem 82 in the outward direction, and the temperature-responsive latch 84 retains the indicator stem 82 against that action while the phase-change cassette 44 remains in condition.

If that phase-change cassette 44 softens enough to release the temperature-responsive latch 84, the spring 86 moves the indicator stem 82 to a latched exposed position. The indication remains exposed after the phase-change cassette 44 cools again, and is reset manually only after the carrier is opened. The value of this behaviour is that a payload which was warmed part way through a journey and then cooled again arrives at a temperature that looks correct, and the contents alone give the recipient no way to know what happened. The mechanical exposure indicator 80 records the event in the structure of the carrier and holds the record until a person opens the carrier and deliberately resets it.

The mechanical exposure indicator 80 does not control airflow. The circulation path is the same whether the indicator stem 82 is retained or has moved to the latched exposed position. The thermal condition being reported is taken directly from a phase-change cassette 44, that is, from the reserve that actually conditions the payload, and no electrical power, battery, or logging device is required for the indication.

## Method of passively conditioning a payload

In use, conditioned phase-change cassettes 44 are fitted to the rigid spacer frame 42 to form the removable thermal module 40, products are placed in the removable product tray 20, the removable product tray 20 is placed in the insulated outer shell 10 on its tray feet 22, the removable thermal module 40 is placed above the removable product tray 20, and the insulated lid 60 is closed. Closing the insulated lid 60 brings the depending indexing rib 62 into the mating channel 52, shifts the removable thermal module 40 into the registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings 50 overlap the side supply passages 30, presses the resilient feet 54 against the ledges 18, and compresses the compressible lid gasket 64 against the upper edge 16 after that registration. Air then circulates passively along the path described above for the duration of the journey.

At the destination the insulated lid 60 is opened, the removable thermal module 40 is lifted out, and the removable product tray 20 is lifted out with the payload in it. Between journeys the removable absorbent wick 72 is withdrawn from the shallow condensate channel 70 by the pull tab 74 and replaced, the phase-change cassettes 44 are reconditioned, and the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is reset by hand if it has moved to the latched exposed position.

## Variations

The removable absorbent wick 72 and the mechanical exposure indicator 80 are optional features. A carrier may be built with the registered passive circulation path and the lid-driven registration alone, or with either optional feature separately, or with both. Features described in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another where the combination is physically consistent. The claims that follow define the invention, and each claim is to be read in the light of the whole of this description.

input.summary:
Preflight source-fidelity review of the p14 passive cold-chain carrier candidate. The ledger authority is a single USER block: input/disclosure.md and the one USER passage in input/conversation.md are textually identical, so there is no second inventor passage to draw on. input/brief.md was used only for formalities.

Formalities are clean. The title is descriptive and consistent with the disclosed subject matter; "Not applicable" for both cross-reference and government support matches the brief ("No priority claim. No federally sponsored research or development."); no means-plus-function language appears; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any draft file; the abstract is ~138 words, inside the 150-word limit. The reference-numeral table is sound: every one of the 30 numerals is used in the description, each denotes exactly one part, each appears in at least one figure brief, no numeral appears in the description that is missing from the table, and each brief's "Numerals shown on this figure" list matches the items that brief actually verbalizes. Terms with a collision risk are consistently modified throughout (tray feet 22 vs. resilient feet 54; central inlet opening 46 vs. peripheral outlet openings 50 vs. condensate discharge openings 56; mating channel 52 vs. shallow condensate channel 70). The section line is designated identically in all three required places: FIG-1.md defines "line 2-2 ... the same section designation being repeated at each end of the line" with rearward arrows, FIG-2.md is "taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 1", and draft/07-drawings.md recites "taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 1". The four unnumbered detail circles in FIG-2.md correspond one-to-one and by consistent positional wording to the FIG. 3 through FIG. 6 entries in 07-drawings.md and to each enlarged brief's opening line.

The claim backbone traces cleanly. Every limitation of claim 1 and claim 12 is affirmatively disclosed: the shell/tray/module/lid architecture, shell floor, shell side walls and upper edge, tray feet suspending the tray so a lower return passage remains, tray side walls spaced inward to form two side supply passages, tray perforations, the rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes and resting above the tray and below the lid, the central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes, peripheral outlet openings, the whole air sequence inlet-faces-ducts-outlets-side passages-perforations-return passage, the "no fan, pump, or powered air mover" negative limitation, and lid-driven registration by the depending indexing rib entering the mating channel to produce the outlet/side-passage overlap. Dependent claims 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 17 each trace to an exact sentence of the disclosure (gasket sealing "after registration"; resilient feet pressed against ledges so the module "cannot lift away from the tray during transport"; opposed cassettes with lower-end duct openings; condensate discharge into the channel; wick and pull tab; the stem/latch/spring indicator and its manual-only reset; "The indicator does not control airflow"). Claims 5 and 15 (module lifts out as one piece with both cassettes; tray thereafter lifts out with the payload) follow directly from the disclosed removability and the disclosed stacking order and are treated as supported. The optional-feature framing in the Summary and in the Variations paragraph matches the disclosure's own "The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features." Claims and description use the same relationships and terminology throughout, and the figure briefs and 07-drawings.md agree on what each view shows.

Eight findings follow; none touches the claim backbone.

One is critical. FIG-2.md still verbalizes shallow condensate channel 70 as a trough formed "in its upper surface", i.e. formed in the upper surface of the shell-floor slab alongside the tray at each side. The disclosure locates the channel only as being "around the product tray" and never says what it is formed in; the wording also places a functional condensate feature inside the lower end of the air circulation path. FIG-5.md already carries the correct neutral wording, so the fix is to match it.

One is major. Detailed description ¶25 asserts an undisclosed misregistered geometry: that displaced peripheral outlet openings 50 "discharge against the tray side walls 24 or against the shell side walls 14". The disclosure describes only the registered condition and never any out-of-position configuration or where the openings then face.

Six are minor. FIG-3.md verbalizes the rib/channel joint as "integral with the underside of the lid 60" and as fitting "across a narrow blank clearance" - a one-piece construction statement and a contact-topology statement for a functional joint, neither disclosed, and the first also inconsistent with FIG-1.md's neutral "projecting downward from the underside of the lid 60". FIG-1.md places compressible lid gasket 64 "set in from the perimeter", a radial position for a seal that the inventor never gave. FIG-1.md assigns rectangular outlines to shell 10, tray 20 and lid 60 without the "shown schematically" qualifier that the same brief applies to its other generic items. FIG-6.md types spring 86 as a "helical compression element" drawn "to show it under compression", where the source says only "a spring". Detailed description ¶9 asserts an untraced result ("Loading and unloading therefore do not disturb the passages ... not by any separate ducting that has to be assembled"). Background ¶1 uses "carriers" to mean couriers, colliding with "carrier" as the defined device.

Background prior-art characterizations were not assessed for inventor support, per the standing instruction; they contain no citations for a later reviewer to trace. Per input/brief.md no prior-art search was run, so the art in prior_art/ may be incomplete. No rendered image was inspected.

findings.title: FIG-2 verbalizes shallow condensate channel 70 as a trough formed in the upper surface of the shell-floor slab
findings.detail: The brief states where the condensate channel is formed and what it is formed in. The disclosure locates the channel only relative to the tray and never says it is formed in the shell floor, nor that it lies at the foot of the side supply passages. Forming the channel in the upper surface of the floor slab beside the tray puts a functional condensate feature into the lower end of the disclosed air circulation path, which is a relative-location and flow-boundary assertion of technical substance, not a depiction convention. FIG-5.md verbalizes the same part neutrally ("a shallow upwardly open trough alongside the removable product tray, shown schematically"), so the two briefs are also inconsistent with one another.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-2.md): "An unnumbered horizontal hatched slab spans the bottom of the view, and a shallow upwardly open trough is shown schematically in its upper surface alongside the tray 20 at each side." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md ¶11 / conversation.md USER ¶13), which shows the gap: "A removable absorbent wick lies in a shallow condensate channel around the product tray." No affirmative passage states what the channel is formed in or where it lies relative to the shell floor or the side supply passages.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md replace the bullet with: "An unnumbered horizontal hatched slab spans the bottom of the view. A shallow upwardly open trough is shown schematically alongside the tray 20 at each side."

findings.title: Detailed description asserts an undisclosed misregistered geometry for the peripheral outlet openings
findings.detail: The description states what the peripheral outlet openings 50 face when the module is out of position. The disclosure describes only the registered condition, in which the peripheral outlet openings are aligned with and overlap the side supply passages; it never describes a displaced position, and it never says that the outlet openings would then discharge against the tray side walls or the shell side walls. That is an untraced relative-location and flow-boundary statement about a configuration the inventor never disclosed. The surrounding point that the path exists only when the openings overlap the passages is supported and can stay.
findings.evidence: Candidate (¶25): "If the removable thermal module 40 is set down out of position, the peripheral outlet openings 50 discharge against the tray side walls 24 or against the shell side walls 14, the descending limb of the path is blocked, and the carrier behaves as a plain insulated box." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md ¶9): "the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame and shifts the thermal module into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages." No affirmative passage describes an out-of-position module or what the openings then face.
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶25 delete "the peripheral outlet openings 50 discharge against the tray side walls 24 or against the shell side walls 14," so the sentence reads: "If the removable thermal module 40 is set down out of position, the descending limb of the path is blocked, and the carrier behaves as a plain insulated box."

findings.title: FIG-3 verbalizes the indexing rib as integral with the lid and specifies a clearance fit in the mating channel
findings.detail: Two untraced statements about a functional joint. "Integral with the underside of the lid 60" asserts one-piece construction, where the disclosure says only that the lid "carries" the rib. "Across a narrow blank clearance" asserts the contact topology of the rib/channel fit, which the disclosure never characterizes. Contact topology of a functional joint is substantive even in a view the brief calls schematic. The "integral" wording is also inconsistent with FIG-1.md, which depicts the same part neutrally as "a short straight rib projecting downward from the underside of the lid 60, shown schematically".
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-3.md): "Depending indexing rib 62: a downwardly projecting hatched tongue integral with the underside of the lid 60, aligned above the mating channel 52 and entering it, its side surfaces facing those of the channel 52 across a narrow blank clearance." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md ¶9): "The lid carries a depending indexing rib. As the lid closes, the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame..." No affirmative passage describes one-piece construction or the fit between the rib and the channel.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md replace the bullet with: "Depending indexing rib 62: a downwardly projecting hatched tongue on the underside of the lid 60, shown schematically, aligned above the mating channel 52 and entering it, its side surfaces facing those of the channel 52."

findings.title: FIG-1 verbalizes a radial position for compressible lid gasket 64 on the lid underside
findings.detail: "Set in from the perimeter" places the seal at a stated inward offset from the edge of the lid. The disclosure discloses the gasket and its sealing function against the upper edge of the shell but says nothing about where on the lid underside it sits. Radial position of a seal relative to the sealing face is substantive under the functional-surface rule, and the brief already carries the disclosed relationship in its later line "The upper edge 16 faces the compressible lid gasket 64." Continuity of the band is required by the disclosed sealing function and may stay.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): "A compressible lid gasket 64 is drawn on that underside as a continuous band set in from the perimeter and running all the way around it." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md ¶9): "A compressible lid gasket seals against the upper edge of the shell after registration." No affirmative passage gives the gasket's position on the lid underside.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md replace the clause with: "A compressible lid gasket 64 is drawn on that underside, shown schematically as a continuous band running all the way around it and positioned to face the upper edge 16."

findings.title: FIG-1 assigns rectangular outlines to the shell, tray and lid without the schematic qualifier
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, Insulated outer shell 10 bullet (line 5), Removable product tray 20 bullet (line 6), Insulated lid 60 bullet (line 9)
findings.detail: The disclosure discloses these four bodies but never their shape or proportions. FIG-1.md applies "shown schematically" to its other generic items (perforations 26, module 40, rib 62) but not to the three main bodies, so as written the rectangular box, rectangular pan and rectangular slab read as shape assertions rather than depiction conventions. The claims and description are correctly shape-neutral, so the outlines can remain as a convention once the brief labels them as such. The plan relationships already stated (tray smaller in plan than the shell, lid matching the shell in plan, bodies aligned one above the other) follow from the disclosed nesting and lid closure and may stay. No shape language should be added to the application text to justify the choice.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): "Insulated outer shell 10: an open-topped rectangular box with visible wall thickness..."; "Removable product tray 20: an open-topped rectangular pan, smaller in plan than the shell 10..."; "Insulated lid 60: a rectangular slab floating above the module 40...". Nearest source passage (disclosure.md ¶5): "A reusable passive cold-chain carrier has an insulated outer shell, a removable product tray, a removable thermal module, and an insulated lid." No affirmative passage gives any of these bodies a shape.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md insert the schematic qualifier in each of the three bullets: "Insulated outer shell 10: an open-topped rectangular box with visible wall thickness, shown schematically, its interior open and empty in this view."; "Removable product tray 20: an open-topped rectangular pan, shown schematically, smaller in plan than the shell 10 and with lower walls, floating directly above the shell 10."; "Insulated lid 60: a rectangular slab, shown schematically, floating above the module 40, matching the shell 10 in plan, tipped in the same perspective so that its underside is visible." Make no change to draft/07-drawings.md or any other application text.

findings.title: FIG-6 types spring 86 as a helical compression element shown under compression
findings.detail: The disclosure says only "a spring" that moves the indicator stem outward when the latch releases. "Helical compression element" specifies a spring type, and "the loops closely spaced to show it under compression" specifies a loaded state and mode. The disclosed function (the spring acts outward on the stem while the latch retains it) is supported and should be kept; the type and compression-state wording should be reduced to a labelled depiction convention. The other FIG-6 items already use "shown schematically".
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-6.md): "Spring 86: a helical compression element in the interior of the housing, drawn as a series of connected loops between an inward-facing internal surface of the indicator 80 and a face of the stem 82, the loops closely spaced to show it under compression." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md ¶13): "If that cassette softens enough to release the latch, a spring moves the indicator stem to a latched exposed position." No affirmative passage gives the spring a type or a state.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-6.md replace the bullet with: "Spring 86: a spring shown schematically as a series of connected loops in the interior of the housing, between an inward-facing internal surface of the indicator 80 and a face of the stem 82, acting on the stem 82 in the outward direction." Leave the following relationship bullet unchanged.

findings.title: Detailed description asserts an untraced loading result and an untraced comparison to separate ducting
findings.detail: The clause asserts a servicing result (loading and unloading do not disturb the passages) and a negative structural comparison (no separate ducting that has to be assembled). The disclosure states how the passages are formed but never asserts either the result or the comparison; "separate ducting" appears nowhere in the inventor's words. The supported structural point, that the passages are defined by the position the tray takes up in the shell, can be kept.
findings.evidence: Candidate (¶9): "Loading and unloading therefore do not disturb the passages, because the passages are formed by the position that the removable product tray 20 takes up when it is returned to the insulated outer shell 10 and not by any separate ducting that has to be assembled." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md ¶5): "The product tray is suspended above the shell floor by feet so that a lower return passage remains under the tray. The tray side walls are spaced inward from the shell side walls to form two side supply passages." No affirmative passage states the loading result or refers to separate ducting.
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶9 replace the sentence with: "The side supply passages 30 and the lower return passage 28 are formed by the position that the removable product tray 20 takes up when it is returned to the insulated outer shell 10."

findings.title: "carriers" used in the Background to mean couriers, colliding with the defined device term
findings.detail: "Carrier" is the term used throughout the title, field, summary, description, claims and abstract for the claimed apparatus ("A passive cold-chain carrier, comprising:"). Background ¶1 uses the same word in a different sense, for the persons or companies that transport the container, so the term does not mean one thing across the application. This is a terminology fix only; the prior-art characterization itself is untouched.
findings.evidence: Candidate (05-background.md ¶1): "A container of this kind is loaded at a packing point, handed to one or more carriers, and opened at a destination that may be many hours away." Compare draft/09-claims.md claim 1: "A passive cold-chain carrier, comprising:" and draft/01-title.md: "Passive Cold-Chain Carrier Having a Lid-Registered Thermal Module...".
findings.fix: In draft/05-background.md ¶1 replace "handed to one or more carriers" with "handed to one or more couriers".

Six are minor. FIG-3.md verbalizes the rib/channel joint as "integral with the underside of the lid 60" and as fitting "across a narrow blank clearance" - a one-piece construction statement and a contact-topology statement for a functional joint, neither disclosed, and the first also inconsistent with FIG-1.md's neutral "projecting downward from the underside of the lid 60". FIG-1.md places compressible lid gasket 64 "set in from the perimeter", a radial position for a seal that the inventor never gave. FIG-1.md assigns rectangular outlines to shell 10, tray 20 and lid 60 without the "shown schematically" qualifier that the same brief applies to its other generic items. FIG-6.md types spring 86 as a "helical compression element" drawn "to show it under compression", where the source says only "a spring". Detailed description ¶9 asserts an untraced result ("Loading and unloading therefore do not disturb the passages ... not by any separate ducting that has to be assembled"). Background ¶1 uses "carriers" to mean couriers, colliding with "carrier" as the defined device.

Background prior-art characterizations were not assessed for inventor support, per the standing instruction; they contain no citations for a later reviewer to trace. Per input/brief.md no prior-art search was run, so the art in prior_art/ may be incomplete. No rendered image was inspected.

findings.title: FIG-2 verbalizes shallow condensate channel 70 as a trough formed in the upper surface of the shell-floor slab
findings.detail: The brief states where the condensate channel is formed and what it is formed in. The disclosure locates the channel only relative to the tray and never says it is formed in the shell floor, nor that it lies at the foot of the side supply passages. Forming the channel in the upper surface of the floor slab beside the tray puts a functional condensate feature into the lower end of the disclosed air circulation path, which is a relative-location and flow-boundary assertion of technical substance, not a depiction convention. FIG-5.md verbalizes the same part neutrally ("a shallow upwardly open trough alongside the removable product tray, shown schematically"), so the two briefs are also inconsistent with one another.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-2.md): "An unnumbered horizontal hatched slab spans the bottom of the view, and a shallow upwardly open trough is shown schematically in its upper surface alongside the tray 20 at each side." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md ¶11 / conversation.md USER ¶13), which shows the gap: "A removable absorbent wick lies in a shallow condensate channel around the product tray." No affirmative passage states what the channel is formed in or where it lies relative to the shell floor or the side supply passages.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md replace the bullet with: "An unnumbered horizontal hatched slab spans the bottom of the view. A shallow upwardly open trough is shown schematically alongside the tray 20 at each side."

findings.title: Detailed description asserts an undisclosed misregistered geometry for the peripheral outlet openings
findings.detail: The description states what the peripheral outlet openings 50 face when the module is out of position. The disclosure describes only the registered condition, in which the peripheral outlet openings are aligned with and overlap the side supply passages; it never describes a displaced position, and it never says that the outlet openings would then discharge against the tray side walls or the shell side walls. That is an untraced relative-location and flow-boundary statement about a configuration the inventor never disclosed. The surrounding point that the path exists only when the openings overlap the passages is supported and can stay.
findings.evidence: Candidate (¶25): "If the removable thermal module 40 is set down out of position, the peripheral outlet openings 50 discharge against the tray side walls 24 or against the shell side walls 14, the descending limb of the path is blocked, and the carrier behaves as a plain insulated box." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md ¶9): "the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame and shifts the thermal module into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages." No affirmative passage describes an out-of-position module or what the openings then face.
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶25 delete "the peripheral outlet openings 50 discharge against the tray side walls 24 or against the shell side walls 14," so the sentence reads: "If the removable thermal module 40 is set down out of position, the descending limb of the path is blocked, and the carrier behaves as a plain insulated box."

findings.title: FIG-3 verbalizes the indexing rib as integral with the lid and specifies a clearance fit in the mating channel

Nearest source passage (disclosure.md ¶9): "The lid carries a depending indexing rib. As the lid closes, the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame..." No affirmative passage describes one-piece construction or the fit between the rib and the channel.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md replace the bullet with: "Depending indexing rib 62: a downwardly projecting hatched tongue on the underside of the lid 60, shown schematically, aligned above the mating channel 52 and entering it, its side surfaces facing those of the channel 52."

findings.title: FIG-1 verbalizes a radial position for compressible lid gasket 64 on the lid underside
findings.detail: "Set in from the perimeter" places the seal at a stated inward offset from the edge of the lid. The disclosure discloses the gasket and its sealing function against the upper edge of the shell but says nothing about where on the lid underside it sits. Radial position of a seal relative to the sealing face is substantive under the functional-surface rule, and the brief already carries the disclosed relationship in its later line "The upper edge 16 faces the compressible lid gasket 64." findings.title: FIG-1 assigns rectangular outlines to the shell, tray and lid without the schematic qualifier
